question: Why can dough made with old or badly stored dried yeast turn slack and sticky, not merely slow?
answer: Dead yeast cells leak glutathione, a small sulphur-bearing molecule that cuts the sulphur bridges linking gluten proteins into a stretchy network, so the dough loosens and tears. Every packet of dried yeast holds some dead cells; that is why it is sealed airless. Inactive yeast is sold on purpose to relax stiff pizza doughs.
move: A dead ingredient is not an absent one: it can still act.
source: Pyler & Gorton, Baking Science and Technology
reference: Pyler & Gorton, Baking Science and Technology, 4th edition, Sosland Publishing, 2008
